scope_note: Daily edition from matching Thursday /new listings: 106 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 56 cs.RO rows, 153 deduplicated papers, and 117 ROI papers. Tier A cards are conservative abstract-only autopsies from the repository parser output; no figure, table, full-text, code, or dataset-release claim is asserted unless the abstract itself states it.
executive_thesis: The September 10 batch turns robot intelligence into an evidence-contract problem. Robot policy papers ask whether imagined rollouts, verifiers, post-training samples, future representations, action frequencies, and semantic harnesses should be allowed to change an action. Geometry papers ask whether 3DGS, LiDAR registration, monocular metric point clouds, pose graphs, and map-assisted drift correction expose uncertainty or degeneracy before a planner consumes them. Driving and field robotics papers attach safety to relative risk, policy uncertainty, vulnerable road-user recall, warehouse routing, and marine-simulation coverage. VLM and systems papers complete the same pattern by testing whether confidence, token pruning, video hallucination detectors, chain-of-thought checks, belief states, and privacy claims preserve the evidence that gives a model permission to answer or act.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Robot learning needs verifier-aware action authority
decision_cards.body: HaWMPO, No Free Checker, RoboDrop, JEPA Policy, FreqFM, and Show-Harness all make a different interface responsible for deciding when a robot action, sample, rollout, or semantic command is trustworthy.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Geometry must report uncertainty before planning
decision_cards.body: VSCP, DCReg, OSM lane drift correction, OmniPoint, and LiDAR diffusion papers convert pose, view synthesis, and 3D features into uncertainty, degeneracy, or transfer checks.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Efficient multimodal systems make irreversible evidence choices
decision_cards.body: TRACE, VIP-Router, video-efficiency surveys, Evidence-Order Calibration, VidHalLoc, CT-SAFR, and Belief-State Engine show that token, cache, reasoning, and belief filters must be tested as admission policies.

papers.title: HaWMPO: Hallucination-Aware World Model-based Policy Optimization for Generalist Robot Policy
papers.fit: VLA post-training - hallucination-aware world models - closed-loop policy optimization
papers.status_quo: VLA post-training can use online robot reinforcement learning, but physical rollouts are costly, slow, and risky.
papers.friction: The abstract says world-model rollouts can hallucinate long-horizon state transitions and mislead policy learning.
papers.hidden_premise: Imagined experience should not have equal authority unless its reliability is scored at the action-chunk level.
papers.conceptual_move: Attach hallucination scores to action-conditioned generated image sequences and soften policy optimization rewards accordingly.
papers.mechanism: HaWMPO estimates generated-rollout reliability and uses a Reward-Soft mechanism to suppress unreliable action chunks during GRPO-style post-training.

evidence.claim: The paper targets world-model hallucinations in long-horizon VLA policy post-training.
It reports LIBERO gains and real-world G1 manipulation improvement from 67.5 percent to 80.0 percent across two tasks.
APRL should weight imagined robot rollouts by hallucination risk before using them as training evidence.

papers.falsification: If hallucination scores fail under new objects, cameras, or contact regimes, the optimizer may still amplify plausible but wrong trajectories.
papers.adversarial: Compare imagined rollouts with physical rollouts under hidden object displacement, long-horizon dependency, and contact-state changes.
papers.thinking_tool: A world model is a source of proposed evidence, not a free substitute for physical interaction.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA manipulation post-training; weaker for tasks whose world-model error is not visually observable.

papers.title: No Free Checker: A Survey of Verifiers for Robot Policies
papers.fit: robot policy verification - verifier availability - verifier credibility
papers.status_quo: Robot policy scores are often treated as if denser, cheaper, or earlier feedback is automatically better.
papers.friction: The abstract frames a trade-off: availability rises as verdicts become cheaper and earlier, while credibility can fall as judgments become gameable.
papers.hidden_premise: Every policy verifier needs its own validation protocol before it can train or certify a robot behavior.
papers.conceptual_move: Compare roughly 150 verifiers by who supplies the judgment and by the availability-credibility trade-off.
papers.mechanism: The survey groups human, rule-based, formal, learned, pretrained, and model-intrinsic verifiers, then asks what validates the verifier itself.

evidence.claim: The paper defines availability as verdict cost, timing, and query density.
It defines credibility as how much a high score says about the real task and whether the judgment is gameable.
APRL should report verifier latency, gameability, and validation source next to every robot-policy score.

papers.falsification: If a verifier's score predicts deployment success under reward hacking and distribution shift, high availability may not imply weak credibility.
papers.adversarial: Test success detectors, learned rewards, and runtime monitors on policies explicitly optimized to exploit each verifier family.
papers.thinking_tool: Before trusting a policy score, ask who checks the checker.
papers.transfer_boundary: Broadly useful across robot policy evaluation; less direct for perception-only benchmarks without behavior scoring.

papers.title: DUET-DINO: Simultaneous Cross-View World Modeling for Latent Planning in Robot Manipulation
papers.fit: cross-view world modeling - latent planning - 7-DoF manipulation
papers.status_quo: Latent world models can predict future visual representations but may underrepresent fine-grained spatial and rotational actions.
papers.friction: The abstract says full 7-DoF end-effector control needs reliable predictions across side and wrist views.
papers.hidden_premise: A useful latent world model should preserve both global scene context and gripper-centric local evidence.
papers.conceptual_move: Learn simultaneous action-conditioned predictions from static side-camera and wrist-camera observations through cross-view conditioning.
papers.mechanism: DUET-DINO uses complementary view information for latent planning over the full action space and compares DINOv3-style predictions with wrist-view dynamics.

evidence.claim: The paper targets unreliable fine-grained spatial and rotational predictions in latent world models.
It reports 92 percent reach, 72.5 percent angled-reach, and 60.0 percent lift success across evaluated tasks.
APRL should test whether cross-view latents predict action errors before final manipulation success changes.

papers.falsification: If gains vanish when wrist or side views are corrupted independently, the cross-view latent may be overfitting camera-specific cues.
papers.adversarial: Swap side-view clutter, wrist occlusion, orientation-intensive reaches, and multi-goal grasps while holding language constant.
papers.thinking_tool: A latent is action-grounded only if it predicts the view that controls the next motion.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for multi-view manipulation; weaker for single-camera or non-calibrated robot settings.

papers.title: View-Structured Conformal Prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.status_quo: 3DGS uncertainty maps are often visually inspected without finite-sample guarantees for a whole rendered view.
papers.friction: The abstract says marginal pixel coverage can look acceptable while view-level coverage fails.
papers.hidden_premise: A rendered scene should expose view-wise uncertainty before a robot uses it for localization, collision, or inspection.
papers.conceptual_move: Treat novel-view synthesis as structured regression and require coverage over a fraction of pixels in a new view.
papers.mechanism: VSCP separates renderer-provided spatial shape from a transferable view-difficulty multiplier, then calibrates across held-out views.

evidence.claim: Pixel-pooled calibration reaches 89.9 percent marginal pixel coverage but only 61.4 percent view-event coverage at a 90 percent target.
View-CP reaches 91.7 to 92.0 percent view-event coverage in the reported setting.
APRL should ask whether 3D maps report action-relevant uncertainty at the view or task level.

papers.falsification: If calibrated view boxes do not predict downstream relocalization or collision-query risk, uncertainty remains visual rather than robotic.
papers.adversarial: Evaluate viewpoint sweeps where small uncovered regions contain the obstacle, target handle, or localization feature needed for action.
papers.thinking_tool: Uncertainty must be calibrated at the unit where decisions are made.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for view synthesis and mapping; needs task-level translation before certifying robot actions.

papers.title: DCReg: Decoupled Characterization for Efficient Degenerate LiDAR Registration
papers.fit: LiDAR registration - degeneracy characterization - interpretable mitigation
papers.status_quo: LiDAR registration failures in corridors and weakly constrained spaces are often detected late through accumulated pose drift.
papers.friction: The abstract says full-Hessian analyses can mask which physical motion directions are ill-conditioned.
papers.hidden_premise: A registration system should identify the unconstrained motion subspace before optimization silently chooses an unstable pose.
papers.conceptual_move: Decouple 6-DoF registration into cleaner rotational and translational subspaces for detection, characterization, and mitigation.
papers.mechanism: DCReg uses Schur complement decomposition, eigenspace basis alignment, and preconditioner-side eigenvalue clamping without changing the original objective.

evidence.claim: The paper targets geometrically degenerate environments such as corridors.
It reports 20-50 percent higher long-duration localization accuracy and 5-30x speedups, with up to 116x in evaluated cases.
APRL should log the physical motion directions that a map cannot constrain before trusting a pose update.

papers.falsification: If characterization is unstable under sensor noise, dynamic objects, or changing feature density, mitigation can give false confidence.
papers.adversarial: Use corridors, open spaces, repeated structures, and dynamic-object scenes where different translation or rotation axes lose observability.
papers.thinking_tool: Degeneracy is a physical direction of missing evidence, not just a poor numeric condition number.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for LiDAR navigation and SLAM; weaker for dense RGB-D reconstruction without the same registration Hessian structure.

papers.title: Data-Driven Risk Fields for Safer End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.fit: driving risk fields - relative risk supervision - end-to-end planning
papers.status_quo: End-to-end driving models can optimize planning while safety priors remain hand-tuned or indirectly encoded.
papers.friction: The abstract says absolute handcrafted risk scores may not capture ego-conditioned planning risk.
papers.hidden_premise: Safety supervision should preserve risk ordering that matters for the ego planner, not only regress a fixed cost map.
papers.conceptual_move: Train a BEV risk field from pairwise risk labels derived from rule-based priors, jointly with map segmentation and planning.
papers.mechanism: DRiF learns static map segmentation, dynamic risk prediction, and vehicle planning in a shared BEV representation.

evidence.claim: The paper converts rule-based safety priors into pairwise risk labels.
Bench2Drive experiments report improvements in driving score, success rate, and collision-related metrics.
APRL should compare whether relative risk order changes the actual planner decision under near-miss scenarios.

papers.falsification: If relative risk labels inherit flawed rule priors, the learned risk field may preserve interpretable but wrong safety rankings.
papers.adversarial: Create scenarios where rule priors disagree with human risk order, rare vulnerable road-user behavior, or map segmentation uncertainty.
papers.thinking_tool: Safety priors should be learned as planner-facing order constraints.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for driving; translatable to field robots with ego-conditioned collision and mission-risk labels.

papers.title: Evidence-Order Calibration for Selective Visual Reasoning under Progressive Loss of Question-Critical Evidence
papers.fit: VLM reliability - critical evidence masking - selective reasoning calibration
papers.status_quo: VLM confidence is often evaluated as a scalar correctness signal after inputs are corrupted.
papers.friction: The abstract says confidence may be structurally inconsistent across evidence-loss trajectories inside individual examples.
papers.hidden_premise: A reliable VLM should become less authorized to answer as question-critical visual evidence disappears.
papers.conceptual_move: Construct question-conditioned masking trajectories and train a post-hoc reliability head with evidence-order supervision.
papers.mechanism: The study progressively masks scene-graph-localized critical regions and measures evidence monotonicity violation rates.

evidence.claim: Native sequence confidence has an EMVR of 0.436, and 92.0 percent of trajectories contain at least one adjacent violation.
Critical masking reduces accuracy by 28.2 points versus 0.6 points for matched non-critical masks.
APRL should calibrate robot VLM judges against ordered removal of action-critical evidence.

papers.falsification: If evidence order improves monotonicity but not selective-risk ranking, it may not replace ordinary confidence for deployment triage.
papers.adversarial: Mask action-critical object regions, harmless distractors, and spatial relations separately while measuring answer confidence and action choice.
papers.thinking_tool: Reliability should degrade in the same order that evidence disappears.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLM judging and spatial QA; needs embodied masking protocols before direct robot deployment.

papers.title: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
papers.fit: GUI agents - token pruning - monotone KV contraction
papers.status_quo: Training-free visual token pruning is often treated as a reversible efficiency trick.
papers.friction: The abstract says once GUI visual tokens are discarded under cache reuse, the agent cannot recover that evidence without re-encoding.
papers.hidden_premise: Token pruning in a trajectory is an irreversible admission decision about future action evidence.
papers.conceptual_move: Rank visual evidence by future utility, instruction relevance, feature novelty, and coverage of operable regions.
papers.mechanism: TRACE forms a nested token order and contracts retired frames into compact session state through monotone KV contraction.

evidence.claim: The paper frames pruning as irreversible because cache reuse prevents recovery of discarded visual evidence.
It reserves budget for native visual tokens distributed across the screen to repair missing spatial coverage.
APRL should evaluate robot video pruning as a future-action evidence admission policy.

papers.falsification: If future targets are not predictable from layout and instruction priors, monotone pruning may discard rare but decisive evidence.
papers.adversarial: Hide the only safe action cue in a low-salience region that becomes relevant several steps later.
papers.thinking_tool: Compression choices should be audited by the future actions they make impossible.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for GUI agents; useful for robot video and multi-view streams after replacing GUI operable regions with action-affordance regions.

papers.title: MotionBlind: Probing the Illusion of Motion Understanding in Video-LLMs
papers.fit: VideoLLM motion understanding - world-model evidence - physical variables
papers.status_quo: VideoLLMs are increasingly used as perceptual fronts for world models because they recognize objects and describe scenes.
papers.friction: The abstract says models can name objects but still fail to distinguish speed, magnitude, and direction in near-identical clips.
papers.hidden_premise: A world-model frontend must read the physical variable that planning depends on, not only scene appearance.
papers.conceptual_move: Use paired clips and complementary yes/no questions so motion understanding requires all four answers to be correct.
papers.mechanism: MotionBlind tests frame order, frame count, and selection strategies, with Instance Accuracy as the all-or-nothing metric.

evidence.claim: The benchmark has a 6.25 percent chance floor for four-item instances.
Open models sit near chance and scale alone does not close the gap in the reported study.
APRL should not use VideoLLM descriptions as reward or supervision unless motion variables are directly tested.

papers.falsification: If newer video encoders solve paired motion variables under robot camera motion, the limitation may be model-generation specific.
papers.adversarial: Test same-object clips with different speed, direction, contact impulse, and camera movement while holding appearance constant.
papers.thinking_tool: A model that sees objects may still be blind to the dynamics that matter.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for video-world-model audits; less direct for static perception pipelines.

papers.title: Geometry Conditioning in an Embodied SLM: Training Controls and Robustness Diagnostics in a 0.8B Hybrid Model
papers.fit: embodied SLM - geometry conditioning - robustness diagnostics
papers.status_quo: Adding explicit geometry to embodied language models can be assumed to improve physical generalization.
papers.friction: The abstract reports inconclusive or negative controls: shuffled training-time geometry outperforms aligned increments under the tested recipe.
papers.hidden_premise: A geometry interface should be validated against physical-layout generalization, not assumed beneficial because inputs are geometric.
papers.conceptual_move: Run controlled geometry-conditioning variants and robustness tests on a small hybrid manipulation model.
papers.mechanism: The study compares recurrent decay gates, token adapters, token-clock conditioning, relative-coordinate policies, and visual policies under held-out rollouts.

evidence.claim: Geometry-conditioned recurrent gates score 28.9 percent versus 36.7 percent when increments are shuffled during training.
A state-only relative-coordinate policy retains 7/10 success under frame relabeling while tested visual policies fall after object displacement.
APRL should require geometry conditioning to improve layout shifts, not just expose coordinate-like inputs.

papers.falsification: If a different architecture or data scale reverses the result, the finding is a diagnostic warning rather than a general law.
papers.adversarial: Separate coordinate invariance, object displacement, frame relabeling, and visual-policy robustness on the same LIBERO-style tasks.
papers.thinking_tool: Physical-state inputs need negative controls before they become trusted evidence.
papers.transfer_boundary: Useful as a caution for embodied model design; not a proof that geometry conditioning is generally harmful.

synthesis.title: VLA post-training is becoming a verifier problem
synthesis.links: HaWMPO - No Free Checker - RoboDrop - JEPA Policy - FreqFM
synthesis.facts: The abstracts separately target hallucinated imagined rollouts, verifier credibility, corrupted demonstrations, future-representation supervision, and action-frequency conditioning.
synthesis.inference: The common decision is to expose the evidence channel that authorizes a sample, rollout, verifier score, or action chunk before optimization trusts it.

synthesis.title: Geometry papers are naming the missing evidence dimension
synthesis.links: VSCP - DCReg - OSM lane correction - OmniPoint - LiDAR diffusion
synthesis.facts: The batch turns view uncertainty, registration degeneracy, sparse map priors, camera-model independence, and 2D-to-3D transfer into explicit tests.
synthesis.inference: APRL should evaluate map representations by the uncertainty, degeneracy, and planner risk they reveal before a robot commits.

synthesis.title: Multimodal efficiency is now an admission policy
synthesis.links: TRACE - VIP-Router - Evidence-Order Calibration - VidHalLoc - CT-SAFR - BSE
synthesis.facts: The papers audit token pruning, cache contraction, confidence monotonicity, hallucination detector reliability, reasoning faithfulness, and hidden-state belief updates.
synthesis.inference: Compression and reasoning filters should be judged by whether they retain the evidence needed for later decisions, not only by average accuracy or latency.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: Recent releases repeatedly framed VLA reliability as action permission under evidence freshness.
frontier_memory.body: September 10 strengthens that axis with hallucination-scored imagined rollouts, checker credibility, gradient-compatible data curation, and action-frequency conditioning.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: The previous geometry line emphasized robot-usable maps and planner-facing validity.
frontier_memory.body: Today adds view-level conformal coverage, explicit LiDAR degeneracy directions, and OSM lane-geometry correction as uncertainty contracts before navigation.

frontier_memory.label: Commoditizing
frontier_memory.history: World-model papers have increasingly promised control, simulation, or physical future prediction.
frontier_memory.body: The differentiator is no longer the word world model; it is whether habit, physics, nuisance, view prediction, tactile force, and programmable state are separable.

frontier_memory.label: Contradiction
frontier_memory.history: Bigger context and richer conditioning often look like the default answer.
frontier_memory.body: MotionBlind questions VideoLLM motion perception, TRACE warns that pruning is irreversible, and geometry-conditioning controls show explicit state inputs can fail under physical shift.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: The repo has separate VLA, geometry, safety, and efficiency threads.
frontier_memory.body: APRL can connect them by scoring when a verifier, map, token filter, world model, or belief state is allowed to change the same robot action.

strategy.title: Verifier credibility suite for VLA post-training
strategy.thesis: Build a policy-training benchmark where imagined rollouts, learned rewards, success detectors, gradient-compatible samples, and formal monitors are all treated as candidate verifiers.
strategy.one_week: Instrument ten LIBERO/RoboCasa-style tasks with hallucinated world-model frames, corrupted demonstrations, delayed failures, and verifier-score traces.
strategy.one_week_probe: Instrument ten LIBERO/RoboCasa-style tasks with hallucinated world-model frames, corrupted demonstrations, delayed failures, and verifier-score traces.
strategy.four_week: Compare HaWMPO-style rollout scoring, RoboDrop-style sample filtering, success detectors, VLM rewards, and temporal-logic monitors on identical failure families.
strategy.four_week_build: Compare HaWMPO-style rollout scoring, RoboDrop-style sample filtering, success detectors, VLM rewards, and temporal-logic monitors on identical failure families.
strategy.success: At least one verifier family improves downstream success while resisting a reward-hacking or hallucinated-rollout stress split.
strategy.success_metric: At least one verifier family improves downstream success while resisting a reward-hacking or hallucinated-rollout stress split.
strategy.stop: Stop if verifier ranking is fully explained by ordinary terminal success and does not predict recovery, safety, or data-cleaning outcomes.
strategy.stop_condition: Stop if verifier ranking is fully explained by ordinary terminal success and does not predict recovery, safety, or data-cleaning outcomes.
strategy.paper_path: Credible verifiers for hallucination-aware VLA post-training.
strategy.asset_path: Paired episodes, imagined rollouts, verifier traces, corruption labels, reward-hacking probes, and real-robot validation logs.

strategy.title: Planner-facing geometry uncertainty protocol
strategy.thesis: Evaluate 3DGS, LiDAR registration, monocular point clouds, and map-assisted drift correction by whether they expose the uncertainty or degeneracy that changes navigation decisions.
strategy.one_week: Create corridor, open-space, sparse-view, fisheye, and lane-map routes with manually labeled pose-degeneracy and collision-risk cases.
strategy.one_week_probe: Create corridor, open-space, sparse-view, fisheye, and lane-map routes with manually labeled pose-degeneracy and collision-risk cases.
strategy.four_week: Benchmark VSCP-style view coverage, DCReg-style degeneracy directions, OSM lane correction, OmniPoint-style ray-distance geometry, and LiDAR diffusion features.
strategy.four_week_build: Benchmark VSCP-style view coverage, DCReg-style degeneracy directions, OSM lane correction, OmniPoint-style ray-distance geometry, and LiDAR diffusion features.
strategy.success: A task-level uncertainty score predicts relocalization failure, wrong turn, or unsafe collision query better than reconstruction or registration error alone.
strategy.success_metric: A task-level uncertainty score predicts relocalization failure, wrong turn, or unsafe collision query better than reconstruction or registration error alone.
strategy.stop: Stop if calibrated uncertainty and degeneracy directions do not change planner risk relative to standard pose and map metrics.
strategy.stop_condition: Stop if calibrated uncertainty and degeneracy directions do not change planner risk relative to standard pose and map metrics.

strategy.title: Irreversible evidence admission benchmark
strategy.thesis: Treat frame sampling, token pruning, KV contraction, chain-of-thought verification, and belief-state filtering as policies that admit or discard action evidence.
strategy.one_week: Build a small video, GUI, and robot-view suite where the decisive cue appears briefly, off-center, late in the trajectory, or only through hidden-state belief updates.
strategy.one_week_probe: Build a small video, GUI, and robot-view suite where the decisive cue appears briefly, off-center, late in the trajectory, or only through hidden-state belief updates.
strategy.four_week: Compare TRACE, VIP-Router-like routing, evidence-order calibration, VidHalLoc-style detector checks, CT-SAFR-style reasoning verification, and explicit belief-state filtering.
strategy.four_week_build: Compare TRACE, VIP-Router-like routing, evidence-order calibration, VidHalLoc-style detector checks, CT-SAFR-style reasoning verification, and explicit belief-state filtering.
strategy.success: A retained-evidence policy reduces cost while preserving answer monotonicity, detector reliability, hidden-state belief consistency, and safe action permission.
strategy.success_metric: A retained-evidence policy reduces cost while preserving answer monotonicity, detector reliability, hidden-state belief consistency, and safe action permission.
strategy.stop: Stop if all cost savings remove rare decisive cues or if reasoning verification does not predict action safety.
